markets.title: Planting the garden before the next cycle
markets.excerpt: The day you plant seeds in a garden is not the day you harvest.
markets.reason: John says crypto is gradually moving from a bear market toward a bull market. He uses his own account of selling FTM too early to argue for patient conviction rather than chasing coins that disappear within days.
markets.note: His FTM trade story is retrospective and self-reported. The new-cycle outlook is his forecast.

markets.title: SocialFi as the route for the next wave of users
markets.excerpt: Onboarding into crypto has never been easier with the rise of Social Fi platforms
markets.reason: John links his bullish onchain outlook to easier onboarding through social-finance platforms and expects an unusually strong next 12-16 months.
markets.note: Public post from the same Melbourne recording morning as the garden/conviction post.

markets.title: Why is Crypto Twitter so angry?
markets.excerpt: The bull run hasn’t even started yet but I feel like Crypto Twitter is the maddest it’s ever been
markets.reason: John contrasts Bitcoin being above $80k in his post with the hostile mood on Crypto Twitter. He interprets that mood as compatible with an early market phase, not evidence that the opportunity has ended.
markets.note: September 24 UTC, following his September dip-positioning posts.

markets.title: Bullish overall, cautious on leverage after the move
markets.excerpt: Yearly open now tapped - good place to be a bit cautious on leverage imo
markets.reason: After saying Bitcoin reached the yearly open in line with his plan, John shifts to caution on leverage. He quotes his earlier September 8 roadmap rather than treating every higher price as a fresh long entry.
markets.note: His description of the plan succeeding is a self-assessment, not a verified trade-fill record.
markets.imageCaption: Original chart: the black projected path is a forecast drawing, not subsequent candles

markets.title: Watching institutional flows, not just onchain attention
markets.excerpt: We are seeing the largest $BTC ETF inflows since October 2025
markets.reason: John points to Bitcoin ETF inflows as a sign of renewed demand and attaches a data chart.
markets.note: This is John’s reading of the attached chart. The research shortlist does not independently certify the comparison.

markets.title: Scanning a cooled-off ecosystem before the next rotation
markets.excerpt: Robinhood ecosystem has cooled off a bit the last 2-3 weeks
markets.reason: John says a cooling period in Robinhood-chain activity is when he would scan and position for a possible next phase, rather than waiting for it to become the crowded trade again.
markets.note: His subsequent PONS setup later broke down; that separate receipt is available if Benji wants one specific example of timing risk.

markets.title: A good narrative can be diluted by five clones
markets.excerpt: Nothing worse than thinking you found the next big cook just to see 5 vamps spawn on every chain
markets.reason: John complains that copies across chains can split attention so badly that the original and its imitators all fail.
markets.note: Standalone September 22 public post. “Vamps” means competing copies drawing attention and liquidity from the same idea.

markets.title: The retest people wanted becomes the dip they fear
markets.excerpt: This is the retest everyone’s been wanting for weeks
markets.reason: John says he began filling longs during the September shakeout because traders had become overly bearish on the pullback they previously wanted. He argues that the macro headlines were already reflected in price.
markets.note: These are his views about what was priced in and his own position disclosure; no execution price is inferred.
markets.imageCaption: Original chart: the black projected path is a forecast drawing, not subsequent candles

markets.title: Allowing for a flush before the larger move
markets.excerpt: I am looking to bid $74k down towards $68k for a move back to $120k+
markets.reason: John anticipates a possible Bitcoin flush around CPI and rate uncertainty, naming an area where he would look to buy before a larger recovery.
markets.note: The price levels and prospective recovery are his scenario, not a forecast from Rubicon.

markets.title: Spot sellers versus eager leveraged longs
markets.excerpt: Spot is unloading & perps apeing heavily What could go wrong
markets.reason: John calls attention to a mismatch between spot selling and aggressive perpetual-futures buying, implying that leverage can make the market vulnerable.
markets.note: September 8 standalone post with a market-data image. Preserve the distinction between his inference and the data series shown.

markets.title: Finding winners and holding them are different skills
markets.excerpt: I told them I’m impressed that you’re on all these early runners
markets.reason: John describes a trader who identified several large runners early but kept taking tiny gains or losses. He praises the selection skill while arguing that fear from the previous bear market was preventing conviction.
markets.note: The other trader’s entries and outcomes are John’s anecdote; they are not newly verified calls by John.

markets.title: Are social-trading apps changing the value of listings?
markets.excerpt: Pumpfun / FOMO are pretty much making exchange listings irrelevant unless your getting perps
markets.reason: John argues that Pumpfun and FOMO are making conventional exchange listings less important for access, while retaining an exception for derivatives.
markets.note: September 2 public post. Pumpfun here refers to the platform, not a disclosed PUMP-token position.

markets.title: Enough new chains and launchpads
markets.excerpt: We don’t need anymore new chains Sincerely, Everyone in the trenches
markets.reason: John says traders do not need more new chains, then replies to add launchpads to that complaint.
markets.note: Two days later he is enthusiastic about PAID’s creator-monetization approach; he appears to distinguish new usefulness from another generic venue.

markets.title: Revenue as the next selection criterion
markets.excerpt: Betting on protocols that will generate revenue will be the biggest winners this bull run
markets.reason: John uses MANIFEST and the coming Mani Markets launch to argue that protocols able to produce revenue could lead the next phase.
markets.note: The wording refers to revenue he expects and a coming launch, not proof that the forecast is already delivered.

markets.title: Connecting creator income with crypto participation
markets.excerpt: I think PAID has potential to be the launch pad that links content creators & monetization
markets.reason: John sees PAID as a possible link between content creators, token participation and payments through X Money. He quotes a response from Nikita Bier. Nikita’s response also asked for an opt-out and raised harassment and reply-spam concerns.
markets.note: Keep the parent visible or summarized: Nikita’s response is mixed, not an unqualified endorsement. The payment figures remain John’s claims.

markets.title: The larger cycle horizon behind the short-term trades
markets.excerpt: 2027 bull market going to be the biggest one yet
markets.reason: John reaffirms a June forecast of a macro bottom before October, followed by new Bitcoin highs in 2027 and a possible move toward $170k by 2028.
markets.note: This confirms his continuing view, not that the entire forecast has already come true.

tweets.reason: John endorses Bluntz’s community and accumulation-range thesis. The quoted post gives Benji something concrete to explain.

tweets.note: Do not put this in the wins montage. The two displayed marks are about 16.6% apart to the downside, not evidence of his realised P&L.

tweets.reason: An August 9 primary source for his PUMP position claim, useful as context for the prior video.
